pr_title: [3.x] Fix nested resources being cached if no-cache argument used
pr_body:
Adds the `p_no_subresource_cache` optional argument to the `load()` and `load_interactive()` methods of ResourceFormatLoader, which is why this touches so many other classes. This ties into the `p_no_cache` argument of ResourceLoader, which went unused for nested resources in text/binary custom resources. This resulted in cached resources not being updated despite the cache being told to be skipped.

I am told this is already fixed in 4.0, so this is for 3.x only.

Fixes #59686, fixes #59752

issue_context.title: Inconsistent base class detection
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues for potential duplicates before filing yours:	
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue	
-->

**Godot version:**
3.2 branch commit 7b4b83e9dcb91b44b39e8cc87df3ddecdb29b689


**OS/device including version:**
Arch Linux


**Issue description:**
Attempting to add custom nodes using `class_name` and `tool` has inconsistent behavior -- some scripts seem to extend `Reference` as the base class when this is not the case.

Before following the steps to reproduce this issue, note that `grid_background/grid_background.gd` in the attached project extends `TextureRect`. Also `grid_background/grid_texture.gd` extends `ImageTexture`, but for some reason both are sometimes detected to extend `Reference`.


**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Open `project.godot` and check out the original `_global_script_classes`:
```
_global_script_classes=[ {
"base": "Reference",
"class": "GridBackground",
"language": "GDScript",
"path": "res://grid_background/grid_background.gd"
}, {
"base": "Reference",
"class": "GridTexture",
"language": "GDScript",
"path": "res://grid_background/grid_texture.gd"
} ]
```
2. Open the Godot Editor with `godot -e`, and when it finishes loading close it. There's a chance `GridBackground` and `GridTexture` still extend `Reference` according to `project.godot`, but if you look at their script they do not. This is the case I'm referring to -- you have reproduced the issue.
3. On the other hand, if `project.godot` do not show `Reference` as the base classes, try the following.
4. Rename `grid_background` folder to `test1` for example.
5. Open and close the Godot Editor.
6. Check `project.godot` -> `GridTexture` and `GridBackground` now "extend" `Reference` at least according to that file.
7. Reopening the project several times does not help in detecting the base class correctly either.

**Minimal reproduction project:**
[InconsistentBaseClassDetection.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/4957483/InconsistentBaseClassDetection.zip)

I'm still not sure what is the root cause yet, but I'll keep digging.

The root of the problem is Godot's cache.

More specifically the file `filesystem_cache6` stored at `$HOME/.config/godot/projects/` which is written when the attached project is opened with `godot -e` for the first time is the culprit, however it turns out that subsequently opening the attached project will make Godot store this file at `$HOME/.config/godot/projects/InconsistentBaseClassDetection-<hash_value>/filesystem_cache6` instead, which then will also cause problems. Deleting this `filesystem_cache6` file at both of these locations allows Godot to detect base classes correctly.

It's important to point out that Godot's caching mechanism is not working properly when opening projects with `godot -e` directly for the first time without importing them through `Project Manager` first. This is because when using that command line, Godot will also cache other files, aside from `filesystem_cache6`,  outside of their corresponding project folders and write them at `$HOME/.config/godot/projects` instead. Subsequently opening projects for the second time and onward, will write files to `$HOME/.config/godot/projects/<project_name>-<hash>/` instead.

I'm not familiar with the relevant code that is causing this issue, and I will not be able to work on this anytime soon either. Clearing these caches works for me as a workaround in the meantime.
Global script cache behavior has been improved in 4.0 so this is likely fixed, so downgrading the milestone to 3.x.

review_comments: I'm not familiar with how the coding standards would decide on this (or *who* could confirm for you), but I'd want to double-check whether output variables should always be at the end of method definitions (in which case, `p_no_subresource_cache` would be preferred to be before `r_error`). On the other hand, doing so would require you to also refactor all uses of this loader in the codebase to ensure that it uses the proper ordering of arguments, so it'd be a lot more involved.
Since this is 3.x I think it needs to be at the end, otherwise it'd be a compatibility breaking change.
Compatibility is the main reason this was made into an optional parameter, yeah.

It's not compatible if addon plugins defining custom loaders have to include a new parameter (it's optional on call, not on override). It makes them break compat with older versions of Godot.
Besides, `no_subresource_cache` is a double-negative, there were discussions about this being bad practice during the API revamp of Godot 4.
I'm also not sure what the implementer of a custom resource is supposed to do based on this boolean: "if true, sub-resources should not be cached". Cached where? Why would they be? Is this about *sub-resources* (which can be from another file) or *built-in* resources?
